analysis:
Reviewed all supplied source, patches and mode metadata against the indexed model and detailed T-041. SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift:119-154 now passes the TTL cutoff to active-store retirement, allowing a newer indexed hit to protect a block whose scanned mtime is stale. Lines 159-164 refresh surviving blocks' mtimes for budget ordering. This is consistent with sliding TTL rather than an observed TTL-policy increase. Unloaded deletion still uses the epoch barrier (138-143); ownership filtering, bounded metadata reads and no-follow directory checks remain visible (229-330). No changes to HMAC names, encryption, account scope, authorization, billing or plaintext handling are evidenced here.
SSDCheckpointFileCoordinatorTests.swift:75-237 adds shared-reader overlap, writer fairness, upgrade/downgrade and cancellation expectations; 279-404 expands cancellation races and randomized exclusivity/drain checks. These tests add no production authority and do not prove the coordinator implementation correct. SSDCheckpointMaintenanceEpochTests.swift:83-88 now ages both disk mtime and the loaded index, aligning the expiry fixture with the new last-hit check.
No concrete regression is independently supported in this scope. Integration must verify SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries' new unusedSince contract, including atomic last-hit comparison and safe refusal/fallback, and confirm that survivors actually receive the mtime assumed at maintainer lines 159-164. The changed shared-access tests also require review alongside SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator and production callers to establish that destructive operations remain exclusive and cancellation releases reservations safely. Those implementations are not supplied here; their absence is a coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control. Relevant concerns are T-041/A-001 cache retention and isolation, TB-007 concurrency, and A-018 availability.
